mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the historical development of the cell theory is NOT correct?

options.A: Robert Hooke first coined the term “cell” after observing cork cells in 1665.
options.B: Matthias Schleiden proposed that all plants are composed of cells in 1838.
options.C: The cell theory was fully established by the combined work of Schleiden, Schwann, and Virchow in the 19th century.
options.D: Rudolf Virchow stated that all cells arise de novo from non‑cellular material.

mcqs.answer: Rudolf Virchow stated that all cells arise de novo from non‑cellular material.
mcqs.explanation: Virchow actually formulated the principle “Omnis cellula e cellula” meaning every cell arises from a pre‑existing cell. The claim that he said cells arise de novo is a misconception. Options A, B and C correctly describe contributions to the development of cell theory.

mcqs.question: Which set of statements correctly represents the modern cell theory?

options.A: 1) All living organisms are composed of one or more cells. 2) The cell is the basic unit of structure and function. 3) All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: 1) Only plants are composed of cells. 2) Cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter. 3) The nucleus is the only functional unit of a cell.
options.C: 1) Multicellular organisms are made of tissues, not cells. 2) Cells are the smallest unit of life but can be created anew. 3) Viruses are considered cells.
options.D: 1) All organisms are made of cells. 2) Cells are the basic unit of life, but some cells can appear spontaneously. 3) Cells can divide without a parent cell.

mcqs.answer: 1) All living organisms are composed of one or more cells. 2) The cell is the basic unit of structure and function. 3) All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: Option A lists the three universally accepted tenets of the modern cell theory: (i) all living things are made of cells, (ii) the cell is the structural and functional unit, and (iii) cells arise only from pre‑existing cells. The other options contain false statements such as spontaneous generation, treating viruses as cells, or denying the cellular nature of animals.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly compares unicellular and multicellular organisms?

options.A: Unicellular organisms perform all life processes within a single cell, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells that carry out specific functions.
options.B: Unicellular organisms lack a nucleus, while multicellular organisms always have a nucleus in every cell.
options.C: Unicellular organisms can only reproduce asexually, whereas multicellular organisms reproduce only sexually.
options.D: Unicellular organisms are always prokaryotes, whereas multicellular organisms are always eukaryotes.

mcqs.answer: Unicellular organisms perform all life processes within a single cell, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells that carry out specific functions.
mcqs.explanation: Option A accurately reflects the key difference: a single cell must carry out metabolism, growth, and reproduction in unicellular life, while multicellular organisms distribute these tasks among different cell types. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because (B) many unicellular eukaryotes have nuclei, (C) both unicellular and multicellular organisms can have sexual or asexual reproduction, and (D) there are multicellular prokaryotes (e.g., cyanobacterial filaments) and unicellular eukaryotes.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: Which statement represents an accepted exception or refinement to the classical cell theory?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of cells.
options.B: The cell is the basic unit of life.
options.C: All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.D: Viruses can replicate only inside a host cell and are not considered cells.

mcqs.answer: Viruses can replicate only inside a host cell and are not considered cells.
mcqs.explanation: The classical cell theory states that all living things are made of cells and that cells arise from pre‑existing cells. Viruses, however, lack cellular structure and cannot carry out metabolic processes independently; they replicate only within a host cell, making them an exception to the definition of a cell. Options A, B, and C are core statements of the cell theory and not exceptions.
